claim: In the experimental [70,80) kcal/mol band the learned channel has a +2.601 kcal/mol mean signed error (n=129, 107 overshoots vs 22 undershoots) and quantum +1.347 (n=129, 93 vs 36); conditioning on the prediction instead shrinks the effect to -1.185 (learned, n=118) and -0.58 (quantum, n=124) in the [70,80) prediction band.
value_found: exp[70,80) band (statistic = pred - exp, degrees kcal/mol): learned +2.6010 (n=129, 107 over / 22 under / 0 exact, sd=3.500, t=+8.44, p=5.9e-14); quantum +1.3467 (n=129, 93 over / 36 under, sd=3.173, t=+4.82, p=4.0e-06). Prediction [70,80) band (statistic = exp - pred): learned -1.1847 (n=118, sd=3.617, t=-3.56, p=5.4e-04); quantum -0.5835 (n=124, sd=3.154, t=-2.06, p=0.0415). SAME numbers re-expressed in the claim's own pred-exp convention: learned +1.1847, quantum +0.5835 (overshoot, not undershoot). Parent-clustered (419 parents) bootstrap 95% CI for the conditioned learned overshoot: [+0.544, +1.841], excludes 0. Rows in both bands: 95 (only-exp 34, only-pred 23); on those 95 shared rows the pred-exp bias is +1.581. Sensitivity: shifting prediction-band edges to [69.5,80.5) gives +1.160 (n=123).
unit: one benchmark bond observation (raw TSV row, 543/543 unique by observation_id and unique by (parent SMILES, fragment_a, fragment_b); no molecule-level duplication; joined n's are therefore observation counts, matching the claim)
method: python3 output/verify_10_weakbond_indep.py  +  two inline python3 heredoc scripts (clustered-bootstrap and quantum-vs-DB join). Reads only data/normalized_views/experimental_benchmark.tsv via pandas.read_csv(sep='\t') and data/source_data/bde_db_full.csv.gz; scipy.stats.ttest_1samp and binomtest; no import of output/analysis/common.py or weak_bond_overshoot_test.py. Cross-checked identical results against the workstream's cached output/results/analysis_table.csv (543 rows, max|exp diff|=0.0).
notes: All four reported numbers reproduce to the last digit from the raw TSV, and the n's and over/under counts are exact (129/118/124, 107/22 and 93/36). ONE SUBSTANTIVE LABELING DEFECT: the claim quotes the conditioned statistic as '-1.185 (learned) and -0.58 (quantum)' while defining the experimental-band statistic as pred-exp (+2.601 = overshoot). The conditioned figures are mean(exp - pred), not mean(pred - exp); under the claim's own convention they are +1.1847 and +0.5835. So the sign does NOT flip: the estimator still overshoots weak bonds after conditioning, it just shrinks from +2.601 to +1.185 (-54%), which is what 'the overshoot largely survives' asserts. The naive reading of the reported text ('shrinks to about -1.19', a negative signed error) would be wrong, but the script value -1.185 is exactly reproduced. CAVEATS on causality: (1) conditioning on the prediction is selection on the estimator, so the shrink from 2.601 to 1.185 is partly the regression-to-the-mean artifact the original script was testing for; the residual +1.185 remains significant (t=-3.56, p=5.4e-04; parent-clustered 95% CI [+0.54,+1.84]), so a genuine learned-channel weak-bond bias is supported, but the two band n's (129 vs 118) overlap on only 95 rows, so the 2.601-vs-1.185 contrast is not a paired comparison. (2) The QUANTUM channel's 'overshoot' is largely a reference-data artifact, not evidence about the estimator: on the 331 benchmark rows that match a raw DB row, quantum tracks the database value (mean|Q-db|=0.158) and is never identical to it, and quantum's exp[70,80) bias drops from +1.347 (all n=129) to +0.777 on the 77 unmatched rows; by contrast learned's bias rises from +2.601 to +2.963 on unmatched rows, so learned's weak-bond overshoot is not explained by DB provenance. (3) No exact experimental value equals 70 or 80 (70 is absent, 80 occurs 9x and is excluded by the half-open band in both methods), so band edges are not driving the result; the [70,80.001) variant is identical. The template's claim-5 two-method and claim-11 pooled-variance~165 checks do not apply to claim 10 (no variance-pooling or ~165 figure appears in this claim).
